turns.assessment: The common failure is lightpath och170, terminating at S24: all three unprotected services carried by it fail together, while svc283 reports protection unavailable. At trx.och170.z, OTU_LOF and a sharp pre-FEC BER increase occur with no corresponding receive-power, OSNR, DGD, SOP, upstream amplifier, or channel-power change. This strongly localizes the fault to degradation of the S24 receiver rather than the optical path; a card failure is less likely because receiver monitoring remained valid.

proposals.rationale: Receiver-local degradation directly explains the BER rise and OTU_LOF at the S24 end of och170 while optical power, OSNR, polarization metrics, and all upstream line equipment remain unchanged.

A channel-specific filter penalty could impair och170 without changing total channel power, but unchanged receiver OSNR and the strongly receiver-local symptom pattern make this substantially less likely.

A partial line-card failure could interrupt all tributaries on och170, but the documented hard card failure should make receiver monitoring silent and mask traffic alarms, contrary to the observed valid BER change and OTU_LOF.
Low margin could culminate in errors, but the documented mode is a slow decline and no prior margin trend is reported; the event is abrupt.
